answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each entity to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where registration cost scales superlinearly as O(n^2). Much like constructing a heavy stone jetty to halt coastal erosion, burning non-refundable stake imposes severe economic friction against identity proliferation. A single malicious ripple in the identity graph triggers recursive validation penalties across the agent orchard, forcing attackers to burn quadratic capital that outpaces any linear coordination payoff.
